log.text: Would we be able to match the dark black areas in tis corridor with a layer of black volumetric fog/lighting to emulate the lighting the original developers tried to achieve with the texture art?

Done, and for the whole room rather than just this spot. The renderer now reads the darkness the original artists painted into the textures: when the room loads it samples every floor, wall and ceiling surface's own colours into a smoothed map of how dark the art is in each part of the room. Wherever the art is painted dark, the volumetric fog gets thicker black. That deepens this corridor's dark band and walls, and it follows the art everywhere else too (22% of this room's area is painted darker than half and gets it). Your flashlight thins it the same way it thins the fog, so you can still see into it. Tunable in the room's settings: strength (density 0.02 now), how opaque it may get (85%), and how widely the art is averaged.

GpuRaster: painted-darkness map built from the room's textures at load, marched into the volumetric fog (at half size, like the rest of the fog)

The same map shows exactly where they are (its brightest spots), so I can propose real lights at those places, matching the original's light pattern but as actual light that moves and casts shadows. When your first clean textures are in, tell me and I'll set up both, so we can judge them against the original in game.
